x: The best running was that of two of our under twenty-ones, Eddie Short and Mike Heard who finished fourth and twelfth respectively. Harry Churcher is back on the Road again and so far unbeaten this year, although pulled out of the “ Belgrave Open.” Perhaps it is because we think he wins quite enough anyway!

Eddie Short was our first man home in fourth position, and was well supported by Mike Heard 12th, Ron Minahan 19th, and Eric Herbert 27th. We fielded four teams and all closed in, our other placings being: F.
In the Junior (under 21) event there were 20 teams and we did well to finish in 6th place. Eddie Short led our team home in 6th position, Mike Heard was 12th, Eric Bishop 27, and Len Bishop 68.
In the Junior race Eddie Short was again our first man home in 7th position, and to gain such a high place in a race speaks well for Eddie's strength and determination.

Eddie Short had Dale Hill to climb (shades of Bert Footer) but ran splendidly, in to Pycombe, although he was only able to reduce the Stagbearers lead by 4 secs., and so on to the Brighton front to see Bill Lucas turn the corner of the Aquarium ahead, to our frenzied delight.

Eddie Short went next and running a well judged race went right away to give us a 40 seconds lead. Archie Bedford was our next and he kept the lead so that Bill Lucas ran home an easy winner in 1 hr. 30 mins. 27 secs.

With the help of Dick Towndrow, and such as Archie Bedford, Eddie Short, Mike Heard, “Ginger” Kennedy and Jack Brown, to mention only a few of our promising members plus the help of last season's stalwarts, I think we shall have yet another successful year over the country.
Amongst his other achievements during this winter season, Eddie Short was fourth in the London University Championship, over 4¾ miles at Roehampton.

We were drawn on the outside but after the initial breakaway Archie Bedford was seen to be lying second and Eddie Short was also well up. The Junior (under 21) 5 Miles Cross Country Championship for the "Savage" Shield was held on December 18th, and resulted in a win for Eddie Short.
Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well.
Eddie Short went off on the up-hill climb to Patcham. He passed the leader and in clocking 21.34 did the second fastest time and gave us a lead of 11 secs. over our nearest rivals.
Bill Lucas won the mile and Eddie Short won the two miles, beating Ted Stimpson. George Powell's win in the javelin, was our only success in the field events side and we also won the medley relay.

Archie Bedford won the 880 yards and also did this same distance in the medley relay to give us a winning lead in this event. Len Adams won the mile, beating Eddie Short and Steve Charlton. Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump.

In the 3 miles championship, the holder, Len Herbert, was a non-starter and Vern Blowfield ran an excellent race to win in the new record time of 14 mins. 49.6 secs. Reg Ruddick was second and Len Marchant third with Eddie Short fourth. The following gained standard awards: 1st class, E.
Eddie Short won the 2 miles with Reg Ruddick third and we won the team race.
Eddie Short lost a shoe but pluckily kept going and Archie Bedford came through to finish a good fourth. Jack Shields and Ken England were also well up and a new member in J.

Ruddick carried on the good work and " clocked " 14min. 48secs. to further increase our lead and with Stan Davies doing 15min. 13secs. and Len Adams 15min. 9secs., Eddie Short went off on the fifth stage with a good lead.
It was bad luck on Eddie Short that he had to retire from the race when well up with the leaders, and we hope that his strain was nothing serious and he will soon be fit again.
Walker 2; E.

Bill Lucas was 3rd in the Insurance C.C. race and Eddie Short was 4th, his usual position, in the London University event, in which several of our members were competing, and Eric Bishop also ran well to finish 4th in the Inter-Banks Junior race.

Owing to the numerous barring clauses our team was well below our usual strength and then Eddie Short after being in the first twenty at the half-distance suffered an injury to his ankle and although pluckily completing the course he finished well down the field.

…is partly explained when we find runners like Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Bill Lucas, Frank Abberton, Reg Ruddick and Eddie Short not taking part in the big races and although we are a club of considerable numerical strength, it takes time to build up a really strong team.…

Eddie Short went off on the uphill climb to Patcham and put up a new club record for this stage in clocking 21.08, and three runners beat the previous course record.

Also on the programme was the Surrey County 6 miles track championship, and at his first attempt at this distance, Bill Lucas did 31 mins. 0.8 secs. to finish an easy winner, lapping all but one of his rivals, which, incidentally, was Eddie Short, who finished in second place.

Walker was third in the 1 mile and Bill Lucas occupied a similar place in the 3 miles. Eddie Short was second in the 2 miles steeplechase, and A. Bergvalds was second in the weight and third in the discus throw.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Jack Brown, John Bromley, Archie Bedford and Eddie Short were notable absentees, and the first three named were included in our Brighton team, with Eddie as 1st reserve.
Also in the 1 mile team race we only had the Bishop brothers, plus Eddie Short, and although Eddie was 5th, our other runners brought up the rear and so we were placed 5th.
At the bell Ross jumped away from John, who seemed suddenly to "crack," with the result that he was passed for 2nd place, and Eddie Short almost caught him down the straight for 3rd position.
We had no runners in the 2 mile steeplechase, as John Bromley elected to run in the 2 miles flat and Eddie Short could not get away from Camp in time.

We had two runners in the 2 mile steeplechase in John Bromley and Eddie Short, and in the early stages John was running well in 4th place. He came a cropper at the water-jump and was carried off with a damaged ankle, which was certainly very bad luck, and we trust he will soon recover from his injury.
Near the end of the winter season, Eddie Short was in hospital suffering from a kick in the back, sustained while playing for the camp Rugby team, and who should be in the same R.A.F. ward but E.

Bedford,our junior D.Baulch,L.Herbert Bill Lucas, Dennis Brickwood, Len Bishop, Eddie Short, S. Gawler and Mike Stearman all of whom were to give the selectors some head aches when trying to find the best team for the approaching National Brighton Relay.

Our next two home were Stan Gawler 98th, and Eddie Short 128th.Both these runners were further back than expected, although in fairness to Eddie Short it must be stated that his training has been interrupted this winter.

We had a competitor in each event except the pole vault which certainly shows the growth of the section. Eddie Short was 3rd in the 3000 metres steeplechase. I am now looking forward to the Kinnaird and hope we shall again make a good show.
Eddie Short was very unlucky in the steeplechase. He was lying second when he twisted his foot at the water jump with two laps to go and had to retire.

Our new Cross Country Captain, Eddie Short, then took over at Purley for the long grind to Earlswood and I suppose no one could wish for a less envious task than to chase Alec Olney of T.V.H. who must be considered one of the best road runners of all time.
We were well back on the first leg, but were brought from 9th to 2nd during the next two legs. Len Herbert maintained this but Eddie Short lost a place which John Bromley was unable to regain.
The lecture on "Body levers" was most interesting and I know Eddie Short was most enthusiastic about it. The "Weight" training session was again most enlightening.
Eddie Short continued his "come back" training to come in 3rd ahead of Charlie Smart. Our sole representative in the Junior events was Archie Boreham who gained 3rd place in his 880.
Jack Brown is to be congratulated on once again getting his name inscribed on the trophy as also are Eddie Short and George Davidson on their 2nd and 3rd placings.

Behind Dave we had a rather large gap, but nevertheless the team were well backed up by Eric Gebbett and Eddie Short. The team showed up well by finishing 7th out of 50 clubs who actually closed in a team.
Next came Eric Bishop closely followed by Alan and somewhere in the forties Eddie Short and Brian Trower side by side. Bob Plummer was about 100th followed by Wally Wortley and Charlie Manning.
Eddie Short did excellently to take fourth place in the steeplechase in a good class field. Percy Luxon was 2nd in the Long Jump and Ash with a 6 foot jump was third in the high.

Our two steeplechasers Eddie Short and Pete Baganll, finished 3rd and 5th after taking a horrible bashing in the process. It is a pity that some of our longer distance track men don't display courage of this sort and help Belgrave to once again take its place at the front in distance running.

In the Surrey Bill Lucas won the 3 miles with 3rd places in the mile by Charlie Walker, the steeplechase by Eddie Short and in both sprints by Bas.
Eddie Short ran well against Birchfield's ace Freddie Green and finally Jack Brown took us to within 5 seconds of winning the event on that last stage with his Club Record breaking run.
In the Junior race Eddie Short was again our first man home in 7th position, and to gain such a high place in this race speaks well for Eddie's strength and determination.

In the Junior race Eddie Short again ran well ... he was our first man home in 13th place. C.W.Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first “open” race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit.

We are sorry to record the death last November of Eddie Short, a regular in our running teams after the war. Eddie served in the RAF where he also played rugby but he got away from camp as often as possible to race for the Bels.

We heard with sadness during the year of the deaths of Charlie Jones, Frank Jarvis and Win Shepherd, who were Presidents of the Club in 1959/60,1966/67 and 1990/91 respectively, and also of Don Brown, Daye Donovan, Len Herbert and Eddie Short.
